subject: Performance assurance: RCA delivery, corrective actions, and closure cadence (Somerset Foods)
messages:
From: Evan Morris <evan.morris@somersetfoods.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Jul 2028 22:04:00 -0400
Subject: Production SLA degradation: high latency and 5xx spike (Jul 21-22)

Irene / Jonas —

We saw a sustained latency increase across our Checkout API last night starting ~21:30 ET and a corresponding spike in 502/503 responses for ~45 minutes. This materially impacted order throughput; our logs show 18% reduction in completed checkouts and multiple customer complaints.

Can you confirm you have visibility and what the plan is to contain recurrence? We need an RCA and a concrete mitigation timeline (including any credits) for our leadership and procurement.

Attached: snippets from our telemetry (summary).

Thanks,
Evan
Director of Platform Ops
Somerset Foods
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Evan Morris <evan.morris@somersetfoods.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Jul 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production SLA degradation: high latency and 5xx spike (Jul 21-22)

Evan —

Thanks for the flag and the telemetry. We’re on it. Quick status:
- We created OPS-5021 and opened a dedicated incident bridge; primary owners are Jonas (runtime) and Kimberly (capacity).
- Initial cause hypotheses: a request fanout change from your side combined with a KV-cache expiration pattern that uncovered an inefficient model loading path.
- Immediate containment: we rolled a temporary routing override at 02:15 ET to shift traffic to a warm pool; observed latency return to baseline within 12 minutes.

We’ll deliver a formal RCA and an action plan by Tuesday 24 Jul EOD ET. Can we set a 30-min readout with your engineering and procurement teams on Wednesday 25 Jul at 10:00 ET?

Irene Choi
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Jul 2028 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident RCA & corrective action plan — Jul 21 outage (Somerset Foods)

Team —

Please see the attached RCA (Somerset_RCA_2028-07-24.pdf) and our initial corrective actions workbook (Corrective_Actions_Sprint_2028-07-25.xlsx). Executive summary below:

Root cause (short):
- Unexpected request fanout to a specialized enrichment service combined with simultaneous cache evictions caused a cascade of cold model loads on the inference fleet. Cold loads triggered additional CPU/memory pressure which increased queuing latency and led to transient 5xx responses from an autoscaling handoff path.

Contributing factors:
- Enrichment endpoint changed at Somerset side the evening of Jul 21; higher-than-expected concurrency (internal and partner flows) wasn't reflected in the historical profile used for kernel selection.
- KV-cache TTLs were aligned to shorter windows during prior optimization, which increased cache-miss amplification under the fanout.
- One autoscaler path had a delayed cooldown configuration that briefly under-provisioned during the spike.

Short-term mitigations (implemented immediately):
- Routing override to warm pool (implemented 02:15 ET) — mitigated peak within 12m.
- Forced gradual ramp for enrichment fanout using traffic shaping (coord with Somerset).
- Temporary increase to cache TTL + pre-warming script for models on the most-affected nodes.

Medium-term corrective actions (prioritized in attached workbook):
1) Adjust autoscaler cooldown and add a short-lived capacity buffer for peak windows (owner: Jonas Weber; ETA: 2 business days).
2) Rework kernel-selection profile for the enrichment model and add guardrails when fanout changes (owner: Karthik Iyer; ETA: 10 business days).
3) Add a pre-warm job to the deployment pipeline for heavy models and expose a telemetry flag for cache miss amplification (owner: Kimberly Park; ETA: 5 business days).
4) Joint runbook and traffic-shaping thresholds to be agreed with Somerset (owner: Irene Choi; ETA: draft by 25 Jul).

Customer asks we can address now:
- We will share a one-time billing credit proposal alongside the final RCA packet (Finance + Sales cc’d).
- We’ll provide a targeted pre-warm before your next high-volume window.

Requested: please confirm the 25 Jul 10:00 ET readout or propose an alternate time.

Attachments: Somerset_RCA_2028-07-24.pdf (detailed timeline & logs), Corrective_Actions_Sprint_2028-07-25.xlsx (task owners & ETA), release_notes_v2.3.1.txt (hotfix applied to routing logic).

Best,
Irene Choi
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

All —

- Cache pre-warm job: scheduled and tested in staging; run for production on next maintenance window (owner: Kimberly Park).
- Kernel-profile update: PR open, test matrix scheduled; target deploy 03 Aug (owner: Karthik Iyer).
- Credit proposal: Marissa will coordinate with Finance and Procurement; draft to Somerset by 24 Jul 23:59 ET (owner: Marissa Cole).

Internal checklist for closure:
